messages.author: 18dec7dfc20b2ae1
messages.subject: Error message from using inla.tmarginal()
parts:
Hi,

Currently, I am trying to get the sample mean and standard deviation of a transformed parameter.

The parameter involved in the computation is the AR coefficient, rho, in the temporal latent effect 'ar1'. The transformed parameter theta = log((1+rho)/(1-rho)).

When I ran the following code
###################################################
## Transformation from (0,1) to (-Inf , Inf) with manual truncation
  to_normal = function(x){
    x_adj = ifelse(abs(x)>=.999999,sign(x)*.999999,x)
    return(log(1+x_adj)-log(1-x_adj))
  }
 inla_obj=inla(...) ## This is the inla model 
### inla_obj$summary.hyperpar[[2]] is the corresponding rho from 'ar1'
 inla.zmarginal(inla.tmarginal(to_normal ,inla_obj$summary.hyperpar[[2]]),silent = TRUE)
####################################################

And I received the error message:
#########################################
Error in seq.default(xmin, xmax, len = n) :
  'from' must be a finite number
Calls: inla.tmarginal -> inla.smarginal -> seq -> seq.default
#########################################

It looks like some non-finite value is produced but I don't understand what is causing this issue. I've addressed the boundary issue by truncating the input before the transformation.

I really appreciate your help.

Best,
Yanzhao

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error message from using inla.tmarginal()
parts: I guess you want to input the marginals, not the summary...

you can also check the internal parameterisation, like

inla_obj$internal.marginals.hyperpar[[2]]

which is the correlation in the internal scale (which you want to
compute it seems)

>   to_normal = function(x){
>     x_adj = ifelse(abs(x)>=.999999,sign(x)*.999999,x)
>     return(log(1+x_adj)-log(1-x_adj))
>   }

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error message from using inla.tmarginal()
parts:
then you know that

inla.tmarginal(inla.link.invlogit, p_marginals[[1]])

is essentially a point-mass at prob=0, which indicate that this value is
driven by either numerics or a weak prior, hence, I would suggest to
revisit the model again. maybe the model is to complex or the data allow
for a complete separation
